mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 5% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a risk-off reaction, depressing near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in the prior month
regime_hint: high inflation or policy tightening anticipation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's mean (t-test p > 0.05) during the same policy regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) coinciding with a declining UNRATE suggests a tight labor market, which elevates expected wage growth and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE declines over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (retail sales) below 1,600 suggests weakening consumer demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (one-tailed p > 0.05) during similar demand weakening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 2% in the prior quarter is associated with reduced manufacturing confidence and negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% from the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with INDPRO contraction (Spearman IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations and typically precedes negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during inflation spikes (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in RSAFS (retail sales) and rise in UNRATE indicates labor market softening and reduced consumer spending, which predicts negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases while UNRATE increases over the prior 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during analogous labor market transitions.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in GDPC1 (GDP) exceeding 2% suggest robust economic momentum, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no correlation with GDP momentum (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it reflects labor market strength and typically coincides with positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (one-tailed p > 0.05) during such labor market regimes.
